thought_title: Christians in Name and in Fact

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Πρέπον οὖν ἐστιν μὴ μόνον καλεῖσθαι Χρις τιανούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἶναι: ὥσπερ καί τινες ἐπίσκοπον μὲν καλοῦσιν, χωρὶς δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα πράσσουσιν. οἱ τοιοῦτοι δὲ οὐκ εὐσυνείδητοί μοι εἶναι φαίνονται διὰ τὸ μὴ βεβαίως κατ’ ἐντολὴν συναθροίζεσθαι.
pass_a_gloss: So it is fitting not only to be called Christians but also to be Christians, just as some do call someone bishop but do everything without him. Such people do not seem to me to have a good conscience, because they do not meet together validly according to the commandment.
pass_b_english: It is fitting, then, not only to bear the name of Christians but to be Christians, just as some do call a man bishop, yet do everything without him. Such people do not seem to me to have a clean conscience, for they do not gather validly, as the commandment requires.

choices.english: bear the name of Christians ... be Christians
choices.why: His contrast of name and reality; kept as a short antithesis.
βέβαιος of assemblies means firm, legally sound; Lake renders 'valid meetings'.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'stedfastly gathered' is weaker than 'validly' for βεβαίως; not a contradiction.

notes: Source shows a spacing artifact 'Χρις τιανούς' (for Χριστιανούς); reproduced as supplied.
Which commandment is not named; no Scripture reference added.

review.notes: Paragraph 1 checked in full. Πρέπον οὖν ἐστιν μὴ μόνον καλεῖσθαι Χρις τιανούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἶναι is Pass A 'So it is fitting not only to be called Christians but also to be Christians' and Pass B 'It is fitting, then, not only to bear the name of Christians but to be Christians'. ὥσπερ καί τινες ἐπίσκοπον μὲν καλοῦσιν, χωρὶς δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα πράσσουσιν is 'some do call someone bishop but do everything without him' / 'some do call a man bishop, yet do everything without him'. οὐκ εὐσυνείδητοί μοι εἶναι φαίνονται keeps seeming and the negation: 'do not seem to me to have a good conscience' / 'a clean conscience'. διὰ τὸ μὴ βεβαίως κατ’ ἐντολὴν συναθροίζεσθαι is 'do not meet together validly according to the commandment' / 'do not gather validly, as the commandment requires'. No scripture clause is quoted, so no verse was required; notes disclose the spacing artifact Χρις τιανούς and that the commandment is unnamed. Title 'Christians in Name and in Fact' names the name-versus-reality thought.

Source paragraph 1: Greek text matches Magnesians 4. Pass A and B both render all clauses: contrast of name vs reality (καλεῖσθαι Χριστιανούς ... εἶναι), analogy of titular bishop (ἐπίσκοπον μὲν καλοῦσιν, χωρὶς δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα πράσσουσιν), negation of conscience (οἱ τοιοῦτοι ... οὐκ εὐσυνείδητοί μοι εἶναι φαίνονται), and causal explanation (διὰ τὸ μὴ βεβαίως κατ’ ἐντολὴν συναθροίζεσθαι). Pass B's 'clean conscience' is idiomatic for εὐσυνείδητοι (see lemmas) and does not alter sense. No scripture citations present; notes correctly state no reference added. No omissions, additions, or contradictions. Covered source paragraphs: [1].
